name: Generate User Stories and Sprint Plan from Epic
prompt:
You are helping a product team plan their next sprint. Complete the following two steps and save results to JSON files.

Step 1: Break down this epic into user stories and save them to backlog.json.

Epic: "User Notification Center" — Allow users to manage how and when they receive in-app notifications.

Generate exactly 5 user stories covering: (1) viewing notification preferences, (2) enabling/disabling notification types, (3) marking notifications as read, (4) bulk-clearing all notifications, (5) receiving real-time in-app alerts. Each story must follow the 'As a [persona], I want to [action], So that [benefit]' template. For each story include: id (US-001 through US-005), title, persona, story (the full As/I want/So that text), points (Fibonacci: 1, 2, 3, 5, or 8), priority (High/Medium/Low), and acceptance_criteria (array of at least 3 Given-When-Then strings).

Save to backlog.json as: { "epic": "User Notification Center", "stories": [...] }

Step 2: Plan a sprint and save to sprint_plan.json.

Team velocity: 34 points. Availability factor: 0.85. Calculate adjusted_capacity (round to nearest integer). Commit to at most 85% of adjusted_capacity. Select stories from backlog.json (you may assign story points however you like as long as each is a valid Fibonacci number 1-8). Fill sprint_plan.json with: { "sprint_goal": "...", "velocity": 34, "availability_factor": 0.85, "adjusted_capacity": <number>, "committed_points": <number>, "committed_stories": [array of story IDs], "stretch_stories": [array of story IDs or empty array] }

criteria.description: backlog.json file is present in the working directory.
backlog.json contains both an 'epic' field and a 'stories' array at the top level.
criteria.testPattern: has epic field and stories array

criteria.description: The stories array contains exactly 5 user story objects.
Every story object has all 7 required fields: id, title, persona, story, points, priority, and acceptance_criteria.
The five story IDs are exactly US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004, and US-005.
Every story's text field contains the phrases 'as a', 'i want', and 'so that' (case-insensitive), conforming to the user story template.
criteria.testPattern: As a.*I want.*So that|story text contains

criteria.description: Each story's points field is a number from the Fibonacci set {1, 2, 3, 5, 8} and does not exceed 8.
Each story has an acceptance_criteria array containing at least 3 entries.
sprint_plan.json has adjusted_capacity equal to 29 (34 velocity × 0.85 availability, rounded to nearest integer).
committed_points is a positive integer that does not exceed 24 (floor of 85% of adjusted_capacity 29).

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent was asked to decompose an epic into user stories and produce a sprint plan.

Criterion 1: User Story Quality (Weight: 60%)
1.0: All 5 stories follow the As/I want/So that template properly, personas are sensible, acceptance criteria use Given-When-Then format with realistic conditions, story points are reasonable Fibonacci values.
0.5: Most stories follow the template but some acceptance criteria are vague or not in Given-When-Then format.
0: Stories are missing, poorly formed, or do not cover the epic scope.

Criterion 2: Sprint Plan Coherence (Weight: 40%)
1.0: Sprint goal is meaningful and aligned with the epic, capacity math is correct, committed_points does not exceed 85% of adjusted_capacity.
0.5: Sprint plan exists but capacity math has a minor error or sprint goal is generic.
0: Sprint plan is missing or committed_points exceeds capacity.
eval.name: Quality Judge
